summary.name: The Two Sides to Google Infrastructure for Everyone Else
summary.one_liner: A Speaker Deck presentation by Gareth Rushgrove, a debate-format talk from Velocity Santa Clara on adopting software and practices from other organisations, such as Google, wholesale.
use_cases: Understanding pros and cons of copying Google's SRE practices
Evaluating whether to adopt another organisation's infrastructure wholesale
Learning about error budgets and feature velocity tradeoffs
Reading background on sociotechnical systems in operations
Preparing a critical discussion of the GIFEE meme
summary.what_it_does: The page hosts slides for a talk given at Velocity Santa Clara, presented as a debate between the speaker and himself. It examines the pros and cons of adopting software and practices from other organisations wholesale, using the GIFEE ("Google Infrastructure for Everyone Else") meme as the central example. Quoted points include that product developers are incentivised to spend the error budget for maximum feature velocity, and that human systems include both a technical and a social system that change together through coevolution. The page text is brief and consists mostly of the title, description and quoted excerpts, so specific recommendations are not stated.
notable: Debate-format talk in which the speaker argues both sides
Uses the GIFEE meme to examine copying Google infrastructure
caveats: Page text is short; the talk's conclusions are not included in the extracted text
Slides are a presentation, not a software tool
